newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity manages gain in narrow session.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity manages gain in narrow session.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures managed to settle higher Monday, erasing earlier losses in a narrow, featureless session, market sources said.
"There's no liquidity and no sense of direction," said Paul Lutz, senior electricity broker at Optimum Energy Brokers Inc in Calgary.
September Palo Verde (PV) futures settled up 11 cents at $30.40 a megawatt hour (MWh) after bouncing between $30.10 and $30.60.
October PV finished up 40 cents at $23.60. Deferred PV contracts ended flat to 35 cents higher.
September California-Oregon Border (COB) settled up nine cents at $22.99 a MWh after traded in a 25 cent range.
October COB finished up 25 cents at $22.55. Other COB months ended flat to 20 cents higher.

Cash market prices in the Northwest eased on moderate energy demand and lower day-ahead offers from Bonneville Power Administration, while those in the Southwest firmed on reduced hydroelectric supply from the Northwest due to this week's maintenance on the Pacific Intertie transmission system.
Firm peak electricity prices at COB were quoted at $18.00-19.00 a MWh, while those at PV rose to $29.00-30.00

The 3,800 megawatt (MW) AC segment of the Pacific Intertie was scheduled to be curtailed to 2,950 MW between 0800-1600 PDT today to Friday, while the DC line will be limited to 2,360 over the same period.
A high pressure ridge building in the West was expected to heat the region's temperatures three to seven degrees Fahrenheit above normal through Friday, meteorologists said.

In its latest six to 10 day forecast, Weather Services Corp said temperatures would average below normal along the coastal region, near normal further inland and above normal in the eastern part of the Southwest.
With the lack of fresh fundamental news, brokers and traders said the power complex will likely stay rangebound in the short term.
"We're kind of locked into a range in the next day or two," a Houston-based power marketer said.
Most baseload units in the West were said to be operating at normal levels early Monday.
The 1,221 MW unit 2 at the Palo Verde generating complex in Arizona continued to coast down toward its refueling outage in September.
The unit, in Wintersburg, Ariz., was operating at 81 percent power early Monday, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission said in its daily plant status report.
